chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who swears an oath, and he considers leaving it to be better, but if he does not leave it, he fears sinning. Should he leave it?
He said, 'Have you not heard the word of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): When you see good in your oath, then leave it.'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they swear an oath and later realize it is better to break it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for one who takes an oath and subsequently perceives that breaking it is more virtuous (*afdal*) than fulfilling it. The Imam cites the Prophet’s instruction to 'leave it' if one sees good in doing so, which Shia jurists interpret as prioritizing the better of the two options—breaking the oath if keeping it leads to greater sin or less good, thereby avoiding the sin of adherence to a lesser good. This ruling underscores the principle of *khayr al-amrayn* (choosing the better of two matters) in oath jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the general expiation (*kaffarah*) required for breaking an oath, as the focus here is on the moral superiority of the act itself.
